report:
The entire new partial manuscript is sound under the explicitly granted complete manuscript O. This verdict establishes the conditional target criterion and its unrestricted-field projective-space example. It does not establish the original P16.4 existence-and-uniqueness theorem. O is excluded from the external-premise list; the unindexed task passage records that grant.

The precise conditional theorem is as follows. Let K be any complete characteristic-zero real-valued non-Archimedean field, X/K smooth, geometrically integral and projective of dimension n≥1, and L an ample rational line bundle of raw volume V>0. Assume O and a continuous psh reference satisfying MA(0)=Vδξ and sup u=u(ξ) for every relative FS potential. For every positive Radon μ of mass V, absolute integrability of all actual E1 potentials, finiteness of the normalized unit-energy bound Uμ, and finiteness of the continuous-test dual J(μ) are equivalent. The stated square-root estimate, finite-dual bound, coercivity and equality of continuous and singular suprema follow. Attainment is not asserted or inferred.

I independently retrieved the literal [BE2021v3 PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3), rather than relying on the ledger. I read the complete pertinent Definition 5.2, model-metric construction and Theorem 5.14 proof, Definition 7.2, Lemma 7.4 proof and Corollary 7.5, Example 8.11 with formula (8.3), and the complete-field covariance statement and proof in Proposition 8.3. I also checked the relevant field-extension discussion and the underlying CLD atomic coefficient calculation.

The norming extension is valid at every point. For a defining FS net u_i↓u, the numbers c_i=u_i(ξ)=sup u_i are finite and decrease. A fixed stage bounds their limit above. If their limit were −∞, u(x)≤inf_i c_i would force u(x)=−∞ everywhere, contrary to the actual-cone convention. Hence c is finite, u≤c everywhere and u(ξ)=c. Subtracting c is therefore a legitimate finite normalization, preserving psh and finite energy by O’s constant law.

The decreasing-closure application is also valid. Its supporting construction can be reconstructed directly: approximate each stage by continuous FS metrics, add a positive error 1/m, and order the resulting metrics by reverse pointwise inequality. Given two stages, choose a later endpoint and a strictly smaller error. Compactness applied to the decreasing closed sets where its approximants exceed either continuous bound supplies a common lower stage. The resulting directed family decreases to the exact all-point endpoint. In the convex-series application, the anchor value excludes the identically −∞ endpoint before finite-energy membership is concluded.

For normalized u, define A_k=∫(−u)MA(u repeated k times,0 repeated n−k times). O supplies genuine positive mixed measures and integrability of the test u against each one, so every A_k is finite and nonnegative. The reference hypothesis gives A_0=−Vu(ξ)=0, and the singular energy identity gives B(u)=Σ_{k=1}^n A_k/(n+1). Affine dependence is used only on the admissible actual segment tu+(1−t)0. Expanding its j curvature slots gives exactly
B(tu)=t/(n+1) Σ_{j=0}^n Σ_{k=0}^j binom(j,k)t^k(1−t)^(j−k)A_k.
Thus every displayed summand is nonnegative for 0<t<1. For completeness, its ordinary power coefficient is
c_r=binom(n+1,r)/(n+1) Σ_{k=0}^{r−1}(−1)^(r−1−k)binom(r−1,k)A_k,
for 1≤r≤n+1. In particular c_1=A_0=0. Higher power-basis coefficients need not be nonnegative; the proof correctly uses the nonnegative mixed expansion instead.

For k≥1, t^(k+1)≤t² and (1−t)^(j−k)≤1. The exact coefficient sum is Σ_{j=k}^n binom(j,k)=binom(n+1,k+1)≤2^(n+1). Consequently B(tu)≤2^(n+1)t²B(u), with no missing raw-volume factor. At t=0 the potential is defined as the reference, and at t=1 the identity reduces to B(u). Zero coefficients are omitted at poles. All integrations use O’s finite-value full-measure representatives, so no subtraction of infinite values occurs.

The implication from all-test integrability to uniformity is correct. If Uμ were infinite, the assumed integrability makes each selected Aμ(u_j) finite while permitting Aμ(u_j)≥4^j and B(u_j)≤1. The reference coefficient 2^−N makes w_N=Σ_{j=1}^N2^−j u_j+2^−N0 an actual convex combination. It is decreasing, nonpositive and zero at ξ. Concavity gives E(w_N)≥−Σ_{j=1}^N2^−j≥−1. Decreasing closure reconstructs its actual endpoint w, with w(ξ)=0, and O’s energy continuity gives E(w)≥−1. Pointwise, −w is the increasing limit of the nonnegative partial sums. Ordinary sequential monotone convergence therefore gives ∫(−w)dμ=Σ_j2^−jAμ(u_j)≥Σ_j2^j=∞, contradicting the hypothesis.

Conversely, finite Uμ gives the asserted square-root estimate. Choose t=1 when 2^(n+1)B(u)≤1, and t=(2^(n+1)B(u))^−1/2 otherwise. This is always positive, including B(u)=0, and B(tu)≤1. The identity Aμ(tu)=tAμ(u) remains valid for an initially infinite nonnegative integral, so the unit bound itself proves finiteness. Finite constants then restore absolute integrability for every unnormalized E1 potential. The raw-mass equality makes the two constant contributions to E(v)−∫v dμ cancel exactly. Optimizing −s²+Uμ√(2^(n+1))s+Uμ for s=√B gives J(μ)≤Uμ+2^(n+1)Uμ²/4. The same upper bound tends to −∞ as B tends to infinity, proving coercivity without a compactness or attainment inference.

The reverse implication from finite J is valid for arbitrary directed approximation nets. Fix a continuous stage and a finite upper bound M on its tail. Then g_i=M−u_i are nonnegative continuous functions increasing to the actual all-point function g=M−u. The dual inequality and monotonicity of majorant energy give ∫g_i dμ≤MV+J−E(u_i)≤MV+J−E(u). No normalized or nonpositive approximants are required.

The needed Radon-net integration statement has a complete proof here. For each level a, {g>a} is the directed union of the open sets {g_i>a}. Every compact subset of that union has a finite subcover and hence lies in one common stage. Inner regularity yields μ{g>a}=sup_i μ{g_i>a}. For a finite layer sum ηΣ_{k=1}^m μ{g>kη}, directedness supplies one stage approximating all its masses simultaneously. This lower sum is bounded by the stage integral and differs from the integral of min(g,mη) by at most ημ(T). Refine the mesh and then increase the truncation height. It follows that ∫g dμ=sup_i∫g_i dμ, including an infinite endpoint integral. The uniform finite bound excludes that possibility and excludes positive μ-mass on the pole set. Since |u|≤|M|+g, absolute integrability follows. The same argument gives ∫u_i dμ→∫u dμ; O gives E(u_i)↓E(u). Passing the continuous dual inequality to the endpoint proves that every singular value is at most J. Continuous tests belong to E1, proving equality of suprema.

The output-measure implication uses O in exactly its granted domain. For μ=MA(v), v∈E1, O supplies positivity, Radon regularity, raw mass V and integrability of every E1 test. The criterion therefore applies when the additional norming-reference hypothesis holds. Its converse supplies no inverse operator or equation solution.

The concrete projective-space hypothesis is established for every stated K and every n≥1. Write a section as a homogeneous polynomial F(T)=Σ a_I T^I of degree m and put C=max|a_I|. At any analytic point y, including points supported on section zero loci or on the hyperplane at infinity, choose homogeneous coordinates in H(y) and let R=max|T_j(y)|>0. The ultrametric inequality gives |F(y)|≤CR^m, hence |s|_{mψ}(y)≤C. Dehomogenizing at T_0 preserves the coefficient maximum. The Gauss seminorm attains C there. Its multiplicativity follows by scaling each polynomial by a maximal coefficient and reducing: the product of two nonzero residue polynomials remains nonzero. This works equally for trivial valuations. Zero sections contribute only −∞ and can be omitted. Since every nonzero section has its maximum at the same ξ, arbitrary finite real weights and arbitrary basepoint-free FS section systems retain sup u=u(ξ). The preceding endpoint argument then gives the equality for every actual psh potential.

For the reference atom, if K is nontrivially valued, take its completed algebraic closure F. If K is trivially valued, first embed it isometrically in K((q)) with a nontrivial q-adic absolute value, then complete an algebraic closure. In both cases F is complete, algebraically closed and nontrivially valued, and remains characteristic zero. The pulled-back reference is the same coordinate FS metric. The standard model P^n_{F°} has special fiber P^n over the residue field, which is reduced and irreducible. Its O(1)^n intersection is one: n coordinate hyperplanes meet in a single reduced rational point. The Gauss point reduces to that component’s generic point, so the model formula has one atom of weight one. The coefficient maximum on every polynomial with coefficients in K is unchanged under projection, proving p(ξ_F)=ξ. O’s genuine complete-field pushforward law then gives MA(0)=p_*δξ_F=δξ, with raw mass one and no degree factor. No discreteness, algebraic closure of K, invariance, support restriction or envelope hypothesis enters this argument.

Harmless source precision: BE’s short pointer to CLD Proposition 6.9.2 identifies atomic support; coefficient identification is supplied by [CLD 6.9.3–6.9.4 and 6.9.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v1). Those conditions hold upstairs on smooth projective space, and the coefficient factor is one. Also, the ordering in the decreasing-closure proof is naturally a preorder; quotient equal stage metrics if a partially ordered index set is desired. These are harmless citation/indexing clarifications, not mathematical repairs.

The original equation boundary remains intact. The submission supplies neither a general-variety norming reference or replacement reference estimate, compactness and upper semicontinuity for normalized maximizing potentials, arbitrary-field envelope continuity and orthogonality, both-sign differentiation in outer continuous directions, strict locality/comparison, actual equation attainment, nor uniqueness of every solution modulo constants. The projective-space result characterizes admissible target energy conditions; it does not solve their equations. The unchanged original P16.4 request and the other original axes therefore remain unclosed by this submission.

premises: For projective X over a complete non-Archimedean field and a semiample Q-line bundle L, the class of all-point decreasing limits of real-weight FS metrics on L is closed under further decreasing nets, including the identically −∞ limit (BE2021v3, Definition 7.2, Lemma 7.4, Corollary 7.5).

On projective X over a complete non-Archimedean field, FS metrics on a Q-line bundle L have the form m^−1 maxα(log|sα|+bα), with mL integral, finitely many sections without common zeroes, and real bα (BE2021v3, Definition 5.2).
Over any complete non-Archimedean K and for n≥1, standard FS on (P^n_K,O(1)) equals the canonical P^n_{K°}/O(1) model metric (BE2021v3, Theorem 5.14, proof).

For geometrically integral projective n-dimensional X over complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued non-Archimedean F, Q-models ℒ_i on a projective model with reduced special fiber induce the continuous mixed dpsh measure Σ_Y(ℒ₁|Y⋯ℒₙ|Y)δ_{x_Y}, where x_Y is the unique Shilov point reducing to each component’s generic point (BE2021v3, Example 8.11, (8.3); CLD2012v1, 6.9.2–6.9.6).
The completed algebraic closure of a complete non-Archimedean real-valued field is a complete algebraically closed valued extension with the extended absolute value (BE2021v3, §1.1).
